Getting Started with panna

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

This vignette covers installation, data download, and basic usage of the panna package.

Installation

Install panna from GitHub:

# Install devtools if needed
install.packages("devtools")

# Install panna
devtools::install_github("peteowen1/panna")

Downloading Data

Data is stored in GitHub Releases. Most load_*() functions default to source = "remote", so you can start using data immediately. For faster repeated access, download data locally first:

library(panna)

# Download Opta data (the project's sole data source) -- incremental sync,
# also works from an empty directory on a fresh clone
pb_download_opta()

Data is cached locally after download, so you only need to do this once (or when updating to get new matches).

Loading Data

Opta Data

Opta is the package’s data source, with 263 columns per player across 15 leagues. It powers the full RAPM/SPM pipeline, EPV, xMetrics, estimated skills, and match predictions.

# Load Opta player stats
opta_stats <- load_opta_stats("EPL", "2024-2025")

# Load Opta shots
opta_shots <- load_opta_shots("EPL", "2024-2025")

# Load all Big 5 leagues at once
big5 <- load_opta_big5("2024-2025")

# Additional Opta data types
match_events <- load_opta_match_events("EPL", "2024-2025")  # All events with x/y
lineups <- load_opta_lineups("EPL", "2024-2025")             # Lineup data
fixtures <- load_opta_fixtures("EPL")                        # Fixtures/results
xmetrics <- load_opta_xmetrics("EPL", "2024-2025")           # Pre-computed xG/xA/xPass

Aggregated Player Statistics

The package provides convenience functions for aggregated player statistics:

# Opta aggregated summary stats
opta_players <- player_opta_summary(
  leagues = "EPL",
  seasons = "2024-2025",
  min_minutes = 900  # Filter for players with 900+ minutes
)

# Other aggregated stat tables (same arguments)
players_passing <- player_opta_passing(
  leagues = c("EPL", "La_Liga"),               # Multiple leagues
  seasons = c("2023-2024", "2024-2025"),       # Multiple seasons
  min_minutes = 1800
)

players_defense <- player_opta_defense(leagues = "EPL", seasons = "2024-2025")
players_shots   <- player_opta_shots(leagues = "EPL", seasons = "2024-2025")

Working with Multiple Leagues

Many functions accept vectors of leagues and seasons:

# Load Big 5 Opta stats
big5_opta <- load_opta_big5("2024-2025")

# Or load specific leagues individually
multi_league <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(
  c("EPL", "La_Liga", "Bundesliga"),
  function(lg) load_opta_stats(lg, "2024-2025")
), fill = TRUE)

Advanced Features

Beyond basic data loading and player statistics, panna includes several advanced analytical pipelines:

  • EPV (Expected Possession Value): Action-level player valuation from Opta event data with x/y coordinates. See vignette("player-ratings") and ?assign_epv_credit.
  • Estimated Skills: Bayesian decay-weighted skill estimation with position-specific priors and context adjustments. See ?estimate_player_skills and ?player_skill_profile.
  • Match Predictions: XGBoost Poisson/multinomial models for match outcome prediction using Elo, rolling form, and team-level skill features. See vignette("match-prediction") and ?predict_match.

These pipelines are built on top of Opta data and require running the RAPM/SPM pipeline first – see vignette("pipeline-walkthrough") for the full map.
